ranking.name: Air temperature near the ground
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, air temperature near the ground in Central Africa changed by +0.297 °C per decade (95% confidence interval +0.215 to +0.381), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.732 °C.

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in Central Africa changed by −0.157 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.234 to −0.082), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is a decrease of about 0.388 mm/day.

ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in Central Africa shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.27): the estimate is −0.0047 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.0132 to +0.0037). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in Central Africa shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.56): the estimate is −0.006 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.025 to +0.014). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water in the topsoil
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water in the topsoil in Central Africa shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.72): the estimate is +0.03 kg/m² per decade (95% confidence interval −0.15 to +0.20). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
